content.title: About
content.content: Low‑fat cottage cheese with low sodium is a dairy product made from skimmed milk that has been curdled and drained of whey. It has a soft, creamy texture, a mildly tangy flavor, and contains minimal fat and salt, making it suitable for diet‑focused eating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, with evidence of its production in ancient Egypt.
Low‑fat versions are popular in fitness circles for high‑protein, low‑calorie meals.
The sodium content is typically under 50 mg per 100 g, roughly half of regular cottage cheese.
It is rich in casein, a slow‑digesting protein that supports muscle maintenance.
In some countries the product is called “cottage cheese,” although traditional Russian tvorog is produced differently.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Provides about 12–14 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, helping to preserve lean muscle mass.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Contains less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, making it ideal for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Delivers roughly 10–15 % of the daily calcium requirement, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt helps manage blood pressure and reduces kidney load.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, riboflavin and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consuming cottage cheese.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein can cause skin rashes, swelling, or even anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although low, individuals on strict sodium restriction should still check the label.

items.title: Quality control
items.content: Improper storage can allow pathogenic bacteria to grow, so observe expiration dates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it plain, add to salads, blend into smoothies, use as a filling for pancakes or dumplings, or create low‑calorie desserts with fresh fruit or berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cottage cheese refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. It stays fresh for 5–7 days after opening. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
